suites.name: CreateCreatures parser and spawn orchestration
suites.method: original PC execution with explicit world/allocation/effect adapters
limitations: World/name/type/candidate/formation/allocation/effect calls are explicit fixture adapters. Original parser, loop, field mutations, scalar evaluator, RNG and cardinal vector helpers execute unchanged.
Zip-up allocation returns null in these fixtures; successful zip-up setup is external, not verified or implemented.
Actor comparisons cover documented fields, not every byte or downstream effects.
Synthetic locator bindings are not the actual level world or source reachability.
Native negative-count loops, stack overflow inputs, nonfinite numeric operands and full hub loader behavior are outside the bounded core.
Compiled C# differential execution remains pending under the Windows execution denial.

suites.name: save decoder
suites.limitations: Synthetic in-memory fixtures only. No user save paths searched, no user saves read or written. These test decoder behavior; they do not establish runtime or real-save roundtrip equivalence.

suites.name: save/audio primitives
limitations: Does not emulate filesystem framing or native save-state machine.
Audio mixer, 3D attenuation, floating-point random pitch/volume and live playback are outside these isolated checks.
ASCII audio config names only; non-ASCII hashing is not generalized.

suites.name: complete AUDIO.CFG compilation
suites.method: independent model compared with original PC parser output
limitations: Covers observed configuration values; no claimtoexhaustall malformed tokens or numeric edgecases.
Native parser emulation haszero preloaded backend samples; file IDs can shift in a full game environment.

suites.name: dispatch lookup and GIT predicates
limitations: Parent fixtures use action-node kind2 completion bits; live gizmo callback values and whole graph scheduling not exhaustively emulated.
Loop predicate verified with no children; recursive reset/walk side effects not validated here.
No complete SCP interpreter or execution of gameplay action handlers.

suites.name: SCP condition chains and action scheduling
limitations: No full gameplay script or inter-script interrupt/state transition emulation.
Condition variable operands, dynamic random operands and condition-bank1 remain outside these fixtures.
No claim that every parsed source file is reachable during ordinary gameplay.

suites.name: SCP state transitions, interrupts and wait commands
limitations: Reference fixtures use explicit target/return pointers, while SetState uses actual native case-insensitive name lookup; source script text loading remains separate.
Mask-based character parameter overrides are verified on synthetic configuration records; their connection to every authored configuration directive is not established here.
Interrupt callbacks with arbitrary gameplay side effects, dynamic condition operands and all action command implementations remain open.
Idle and ResetTimer scalar/time/frame/random variants use bounded ordinary numeric tokens; arbitrary expression evaluation, malformed arguments and all floating-point bit patterns are not covered.

suites.name: named message commands and puzzle-state chains
suites.method: original PC execution with bounded CRT formatting adapter
limitations: ASCII names only; embedded NUL and overlong names already containing msg_ are excluded because original sprintf lacks a bound on that branch.
GIT SetAIMessage requires a valid registry, name and available record. Original handler dereferences a failed lookup; portable source will explicitly reject that invalid input.
Registry lifecycle/allocation/reset and inter-level message persistence are not established by these isolated fixtures.
Native reference fixtures are not a compiled C# differential pass.

suites.name: SetScriptState self/group binding and scheduler chains
suites.method: original PC execution with named-character lookup adapter
limitations: Synthetically resolved script/state lists, not runtime source attachment or whole-level reachability.
Selected group records are required to have a valid packet and base-script pointer; original group path lacks the self-path null checks.
Numeric group fixtures are finite values within int32 conversion range; NaN/infinity/overflow are excluded.
Compiled C# differential execution remains pending.

suites.name: scene/gizmo visibility commands and NuSpecial callbacks
suites.method: original PC execution with synthetic type registry and actual NuSpecial callbacks
limitations: Synthetic category labels for authored type= arguments use NuSpecial callbacks to validate command dispatch; distinct GizForce/GizObstacle/etc physical implementations are not validated.
Dynamic scene fallback global 0x97388c is zero; external named fallback function 0x5c1300 remains outside scope.
Static scene and dynamic scene branches are tested separately, with at most three name entries, first duplicate match and current scene binding.
Compiled C# differential execution pending.

suites.name: compact condition readers, initializers and comparisons
suites.method: original PC execution with explicit named-object initializer adapter
limitations: World global updates, reference lifetime, range computation, off-screen timer accumulation and alive-count population are external input contracts, not recovered by these readers.

Literal NumInSetAlive initializer admits 1..16 or myset; myset reads an unchecked byte index. Fixtures use a synthetic 256-byte backing region and do not assert the actual global count-table allocation size.
All scalar reader checks compare values at the float32 storage boundary used by the native SCP evaluator; signaling NaN payload behavior is excluded.
Eight symbolic comparison RHS occurrences and one malformed gotoUpdate occurrence retain separate source/loader gaps; their condition bodies were still exercised.
Compiled C# differential execution pending.

suites.name: GIT scheduling, Loop resets, timers and puzzle actions
limitations: Graph DAG scheduling model covers action/condition nodes and timer callbacks, not every gizmo or arbitrary cyclic scheduler graph.

A Timer/Action/Loop cycle, including actual initialization, was checked for270 frames at each of four durations, including generation wrap. Other real puzzle topologies and non-timer gizmos remain unverified.
Reset/monitor side effects on real non-timer gizmos remain unverified.
Synthetic runtime records were constructed from native layouts; no original GIT text-loader emulation or full level simulation is implied.

suites.name: GIT saved state and physical callbacks
limitations: Saved-state tests use at most the 512 nodes representable by each 16-word bit plane; larger counts are not treated as safe native input.
Physical fixtures exercise NuSpecial with one static scene instance and animation control; other gizmo types, skinned-instance visibility and renderer/collision refresh remain outside this suite.
Native loader name rebinding is invoked only on empty/previously bound synthetic lists; shipped text loading and editor Collapse flattening remain open.

suites.name: AI2 base navigation
limitations: Tests base routes with selected-route index255 and exclusion mask0. Named subroute groups and dynamic special transforms are not covered.
Runtime records are materialized from bounded decoded fields; this does not itself execute or validate every branch of the AI2 loader.
Live character capability filters, collision steering and dynamic graph updates remain separate.

suites.name: TER geometry and collision math
limitations: These are bounded triangle, transform, deflection and no-hit response checks. Full swept ellipsoid broadphase/edge handling/moving-platform contacts remain incompletely tested.
Runtime query fixtures are constructed from decoded TER fields; original file-loader execution is not implied.
Native coordinates are preserved; no physical meter scale established.

suites.name: moving-platform carry proposals
suites.method: original PC execution with no-hit fixtures
limitations: Only Y-axis platform rotations with nonuniform scale were sampled; arbitrary 3D rotations and singular matrices are untested.
Negative candidate header is a bounded fixture to bypass contact geometry; the recovered transform does not itself prove live moving-platform collision or carry acceptance.

confidence: A check count measures these bounded fixtures, not percentage of the game recovered. Carrier layout, source associations, native caller flow and isolated runtime execution remain distinct evidence classes.
remaining: Full live gameplay runtime and individual command semantics

externalCommandContracts.name: Kill
externalCommandContracts.scope: Bounded command selection and dispatch only; name/reference/numeric services and downstream parts/death effects remain explicit boundaries.
limits: Standalone command with valid script and allocated contiguous actor pool. Malformed tokens without required separators are outside bounds.
Name/reference lookup callbacks are explicit fixture adapters, not reconstructed world binding.
Parts and death cleanup are captured dispatches; no downstream death, FX, audio, stud or body-part behavior is asserted.
Numeric evaluator has original PC finite literal/parameter execution; portable command uses an explicit numeric service.
Instruction audit corrects misleading pseudocode: single and pool paths all reject unordered NaN spawn timers when check_if_dead is enabled.
Authored commands execute against documented synthetic world bindings, not their live levels.
Managed opponent and pool references assume stable canonical bindings during service callbacks; callback mutation of native weak slots or pool membership is outside the contract.

externalCommandContracts.name: CnxController
externalCommandContracts.countQualification: Eight pool-sequence aggregate checks overlap their underlying 528 pool checks; this external total is not an independent-case count and is excluded from gameplay totals.
externalCommandContracts.scope: Bounded command parsing, constructor, connection matching, pool/list operations, frame-mask building and controller update. World target/path bindings and generic gizmo-output callbacks are explicit adapters; no live pathfinder or locomotion.
limits: Synthetic world/locator/target bindings, not whole-level reachability.
Bounded finite numeric fields, valid target pointers, NUL-terminated byte strings and on_frames suffix shorter than native64-byte buffer.
Update fixtures require end frame>=1 and a nonnull connection; observed invalid fake-ID/null-connection constructor behavior is recorded but not executed in updater.
No live navigation/pathfinder or character locomotion.
Compiled portable execution must be reported separately.
